title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves that, read in pairs, the tape at each turn is a binary word and one round trip of the head is one XOR sweep of it: find the rightmost 00, flip the letter left of it, replace every letter right of it by the XOR of itself and its right neighbour, append 11 (mstep_ok). A halt needs a 00 only at the very left end. The block of 111110 words enters the sweep only through its length mod 3 (zone_step), so Lean drops it: the machine halts from blank tape iff the zone orbit halts (halts_iff_zone), and compiled evaluation runs that orbit through the first 1.7·1015 steps without a halt. Since the last arrival the tape holds a new zone, a stranded block of 8,397 letters and the old zone at the left end. By the Lean lemmas the old zone moves only when a sweep gets through the new zone, and for as long as the block lasts it then moves exactly as it would alone: run alone it has no reset and no halt in the 8,397 ticks the block covers. In 3·1010 sweeps from zone step 3·107 only 23 sweeps got through (about 7 per factor of 10). Run a whole period at a time (lean/Window.lean), the cascade gives no halt in the first 1.5·1039 steps (compiled evaluation, lean/WindowRun.lean), and the C engine runs it for 3·277 sweeps without a halt or a reset.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The halting pattern
claims.text: 0 0 1 D> 0, the pass on the separator right of a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left, halts three steps later (F reads 0). By the table this is the only way to halt after the first step (hand argument in the README).

claims.title: The pass
claims.text: Moving left from separator to separator, the pass cuts a block of length k+3 into k+1 and 1 and goes on (pass_split); a block of length 1 stops it (pass_stop). For all lengths and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: Crossing the block of words does not depend on its length
claims.text: The pass crosses n words 111110 in 6n steps, in the same state, turning each into 1110 10; the sweep back turns them into 111110 again. For every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The pass machine
claims.text: A turn configuration RT out rest (C on a pair 11, the pairs out to its left, the cells rest to its right). One macro step mstep: a left pass over the pairs (scanF: skip 11; after a 01, a 11 becomes 01 and the pass goes on, a 01 becomes 11 and the head turns), the three ways of running off the left end (E0 = 1RA adds a pair 01 with a blank first cell), and a right pass over the cells (apass: a1 → (¬a)1, 10 bounces, 00 ends). mstep_sound: for all lists, the machine goes from RT out rest to the configuration mstep names in exactly the steps it names, or halts there.

claims.title: Halting is exactly a question about the orbit
claims.text: orbT k: the k-th turn configuration from blank tape with its step count (orbT_sound). halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some macro step of the orbit halts.

claims.title: No halt in the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps
claims.text: The first 20,000 macro steps of the orbit, evaluated by compiled code: no halt, more than 4·10<sup>8</sup> machine steps (through the first six resets of the left end).

claims.title: One round trip is one XOR sweep
claims.text: At a turn at the right end, read in pairs, the tape is a binary word. When it has a 00, one macro step is exactly one sweep: the rightmost 00 is found, the letter left of it is flipped, every letter right of it becomes the XOR of itself and its right neighbour, and 11 is appended (4d + 12 steps, d the depth of the 00). A 00 only at the very left end halts; no 00 at all is a reset at the left end.

claims.title: The leftmost-zone reduction
claims.text: For every length of the block of words the sweep does the same thing to the rest of the word; the length enters only mod 3, through one letter (zone_step). A sweep that finds its 00 early leaves everything further left untouched (swr_append_ok), and a sweep through a stretch without 00 acts beyond it only through the stretch’s last letter (swr_split).
claims.where: lean/Xor.lean (the same file for the four machines with this block)

claims.title: Halting is a question about the zone orbit
claims.text: The zone orbit keeps only the count of the block of words and the rest of the word; it uses the sweep at the right end and the pass machine at the left end. The machine halts from blank tape if and only if the zone orbit halts.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.7·10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: 3·10<sup>7</sup> steps of the zone orbit, evaluated by compiled code, without a halt; they cover more than 1.7·10<sup>15</sup> machine steps.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>11</sup> steps; the arrivals at the left end
claims.text: The real machine runs 10<sup>11</sup> steps without a halt. Passes reached the left end of the tape at triggers 1, 4, 7, 12, 18, 24, 45, 2384 and 8520 (step 143,858,957). At the last one the zone started again at the right end and a block of about 2,820 words stayed behind.

claims.title: The reduced system
claims.text: With the growing block cut to 10 words at every trigger (cutting whole words keeps the length mod 3, so by zone_step the cut is exact between arrivals at the left end), the run from trigger 20,000 to 1,073,741,824 has no halt and no arrival at the left end; the deepest pass came within 65 cells of it.

claims.title: The leftmost zone alone
claims.text: The leftmost zone run by itself, one arriving pass at a time, from the real configuration of trigger 100, reproduces the real arrival of trigger 8520 (same new cells, same blocks afterwards). Continued, this model halts in its tick 4,581,101 after 19 more arrivals. That is not a prediction for the machine: after trigger 8520 the old zone gets a pass only when the new zone lets one through (32 of them by trigger 5,165,364, fewer than 64 by trigger 3·10<sup>8</sup>; the model needs about 4.6 million), and the block between the two zones is being used up, which the model does not describe.

claims.title: Halting needs the left end
claims.text: Every halt of the macro step happens at the left end of the word: a sweep halts exactly when the only 00 of the word is at its very left end, and the other halting cases of the pass machine are passes that run off the left end.

claims.title: Two zones
claims.text: Since the last arrival the tape holds a new zone, a stranded block of 8,397 letters and the old zone at the left end. By the Lean lemmas the old zone moves only when a sweep gets through the new zone, and for as long as the block lasts it then moves exactly as it would alone: run alone it has no reset and no halt in the 8,397 ticks the block covers. In 3·10<sup>10</sup> sweeps from zone step 3·10<sup>7</sup> only 23 sweeps got through (about 7 per factor of 10). The old zone moving as if alone while the block lasts is a hand argument from the Lean lemmas (the cells that can differ spread from the new zone by at most one per sweep that reaches the block), checked against the zone orbit at all 23 passes of a run of 3·10<sup>10</sup> sweeps.
claims.where: c/xs.c, c/z1.c in the folder of 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1LA1LC_---1LA, from the state written by lean/DumpState.lean; README.md

claims.title: The cascade a period at a time
claims.text: A cell is back to its bit after a list of events or after two copies of it, so the events that enter cell m during the first 3·2<sup>d</sup> sweeps can be built cell by cell (one or two passes each, d the number of cells that needed two). Run through the rest of the word, they give every event that leaves it in that window.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.5·10<sup>39</sup> steps
claims.text: At zone step 3·10<sup>7</sup>, the word cut after 135 cells has a window of 3·2<sup>63</sup> sweeps and nothing leaves the word in it: no halt and no reset. Every sweep takes at least 4n steps, n the block count.

claims.title: Windows up to 3·2<sup>77</sup> sweeps
claims.text: Cut after 161 cells, the window is 3·2<sup>77</sup> sweeps: nothing leaves the word. The 79 events that reach the old zone in it are all background, so the old zone has so far moved exactly as alone. The background events come about 1.35 per doubling of the window, the front of the disturbance moves about 3.3 cells per doubling (cell 255 at d = 77). If both speeds hold, the front reaches the old zone at d ≈ 2,600, after about 3,500 background events, before the 9,947 the old zone alone needs to let a sweep through.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts if a pass reaches the leftmost block while that block is a lone 1 with blank tape on its left; nothing known forces or forbids that.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD1RB_1LF0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A zone of about a hundred cells is rewritten again and again by passes coming from the right, where a block of 111110 words keeps growing. The machine stops only if a pass gets through the whole zone and finds a lone 1 at the very left end of the tape. The last pass to get there did so at step 143,858,957 and did not stop the machine.

facts.text: The halting pattern: a pass meets a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left.
Crossing the block of words is proved not to depend on its length.
No halt, by compiled evaluation of the cascade a period at a time (Lean).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.605).
After 109 steps the tape spans 58,407 cells (19 left of the start, 45,037 right), with a density of 1s of 0.733.

sections.heading: From a tape to a small counter
html: <div class="col">

The question is whether this machine, started on a blank tape, ever halts. Nobody knows yet, but the run can be described exactly by smaller and smaller systems, each one proved in Lean to halt exactly when the one below it halts. This section is the map; each later section explains one step on it, with something to try.
<ol class="ladder">

• The tape

    Cells of 0 and 1, a head in one of six states. This is the machine itself (the simulator above).

    read in pairs at each turn at the right end Kernel

• A word

    A string of letters, one per pair of cells: 11 is 1, 01 is 0. About half as long as the tape.

    one round trip of the head = one XOR sweep Kernel

• The XOR sweep

    A four-line rule that turns one word into the next. No states, no head: just the word.

    the long block at the right end matters only through its length mod 3 Kernel

• The zone orbit

    A short word, the zone, plus one number, the length of the block. This is what Lean runs, and what your browser runs below: to 1.8·1015 machine steps in a second or two.

    a reset splits the zone in two Computed

• Two zones

    An old zone frozen at the left end, behind a stranded block, and a new zone that has to get through the block before anything can happen there.

The panel shows one moment of the real run at the first four layers at once. Pick a turn (the head coming back to the right end of the tape) and read it down: the cells, the letters those cells spell, the same letters split into zone, block and head, and the two numbers the zone orbit keeps.

sections.heading: Reading the tape as a word
html: <div class="col">

Watch the simulator for a while and one moment keeps coming back: the head arrives at the right end of the tape, in state C, with blank tape to its right. Call this a turn. At every turn the tape, read two cells at a time from the right end, is made of the pairs 11 and 01 only. So it can be written as a word: 11 is the letter 1 and 01 the letter 0. The head sits on the first cell of the last pair, which is always 11, so a word always ends in 1.

Why should anyone believe this pairing is the right way to look? Because Lean proves it. lean/Sweep.lean defines a macro step on words: the left pass (states D and its partners crossing the pairs to the left), the turn, and the right pass back, including the rare passes that run off the left end. mstep_sound proves, for every word, that the machine does exactly what the macro step says, step count included. From that, halts_iff (lean/Reduce.lean) says: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of words from the blank tape reaches a halting macro step. From here on the tape is gone; only words are left. Kernel
An earlier check ran that orbit of words by compiled evaluation through the first 4·108 machine steps (blank_runs_orbit, lean/OrbitRun.lean). native_decide The zone orbit below goes much further.

sections.heading: One round trip is one XOR sweep
html: <div class="col">
The macro step is long, but on the words that occur at turns it does something very simple. mstep_ok (lean/Bits.lean) proves that one round trip of the head is one XOR sweep of the word: Kernel

1. find the rightmost 00 in the word;
  2. flip the letter just left of it;
  3. replace every letter right of the 00 by itself XOR its right-hand neighbour;
  4. append a 1 (the new pair 11 the head leaves at the right end).

The machine takes exactly 4·d + 12 steps for it, where d is the number of letters right of the 00. In machine terms: the left pass crosses the pairs until it finds two 01 in a row, turns there, and the way back rewrites every pair it crosses.

Two outcomes are not covered. If the only 00 is the first two letters of the word, there is nothing left of it to flip: the pass meets the left end of the tape and the machine halts (mstep_halt). If there is no 00 at all, the pass runs off the left end and the machine does something else for a while (a reset); Lean then falls back on the full macro step. So a halt needs a sweep that gets all the way to the left end of the word.
Try it. Load a turn of the real run, or type any word ending in 1, and step through the four stages. The last line runs the real machine on that word and compares.
sections.html_after: One more property drives everything below, and the XOR row shows it: a letter changes only through itself and its right neighbour. Whatever lies left of the 00 is not touched at all (swr_append_ok), and a sweep that runs through a stretch without 00 changes that stretch to its XOR differences and passes on only its last letter (swr_split, xd_append). Information moves left by at most one letter per sweep. Kernel

sections.heading: The block forgets its length
html: <div class="col">

At the right end of every word sits a long, regular stretch: …110110110, followed by the head’s 1. On the tape this is the block of words 111110 that the simulator shows growing (each letter is two cells, so 110 is 11 11 01, the six cells 111101, which is 111110 read from another starting point). It grows by one letter per sweep, and it is most of the tape: after 3·107 sweeps it has 29,991,481 letters, against a few hundred or thousand for everything else.

Every sweep crosses the whole block, because the block has no 00. Crossing it replaces each letter by its XOR with the next. For the pattern 110 repeated, the XOR differences are 011 repeated: the same pattern, moved by one place. So after a sweep the block is again a block, one letter longer, and all the zone on its left ever sees of it is one letter, the leftmost one. That letter is fixed by the length of the block mod 3.

Lean’s zone_step (lean/Xor.lean) says exactly this for every length: a sweep of «zone, block of length n + 1» is the sweep of «zone, one letter pat(n)», with the block put back in front. Kernel The panel sweeps one zone next to four blocks of consecutive lengths; the zones that come out agree whenever the lengths agree mod 3.

sections.heading: The zone orbit
html: <div class="col">

Drop the block and keep its length. What remains is the zone orbit: a state is a number n (the block’s length) and a short word Z (the zone). One step sweeps Z with the one letter pat(n) on its right and adds 1 to n; a step costs 4·(n + d) + 12 machine steps. When a sweep finds no 00 in the zone, the orbit hands that one step to the real macro step and splits the block off again afterwards.

halts_iff_zone (lean/Zone.lean) proves: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the zone orbit halts. Kernel This is an exact reduction, not a model. And because a step of the zone orbit costs time proportional to the zone, not the tape, it can be run very far: compiled evaluation in Lean runs it for 3·107 steps, which covers the first 1.7·1015 machine steps, with no halt (zone_runs, lean/ZoneRun.lean). native_decide

The panel runs the same orbit in your browser, written separately in JavaScript. It agrees with the real machine at every turn of the first 3,000, and its state at step 3·107 (machine step 1.80·1015, block of 29,991,481 letters) is letter for letter the one Lean computes; tools/tests/test_tools.py checks both. Computed

What to look for. Most sweeps stop a few letters into the zone, next to the block: that is the left panel of the two pictures, busy in every row. Deeper sweeps are rarer and rarer, like the higher digits of a counter, which is the staircase in the depth plot. Now and then a sweep finds no 00 at all and reaches the left end of the tape; in this run that happens at zone steps 1, 6, 10, 16, 43 and 8,517, none of them a halt. After the last one, at zone step 8,517 (machine step 143,910,078), the left end of the tape changes only 37 more times before zone step 3·107: those are the rows of the right-hand picture and the tall spikes of the depth plot, sweeps that got through the new zone and found their 00 thousands of letters further left. They come rarer and rarer: the last three all come after zone step 1.3·107. Hover a row of a picture to see its zone step.

sections.heading: Two zones and a stranded block
html: <div class="col">

Why does the left end go quiet? At a reset the zone is rebuilt from the right end of the tape, and the letters the old zone had collected stay behind. From then on the word reads, from the left end: the old zone, a long stranded block (the pattern 110 again, with no 00), the new zone, the growing block and the head. The bar above the depth plot shows these parts, measured live from the orbit.

By the lemmas of the XOR sweep, the old zone moves only when a sweep gets through the whole new zone (swr_append_ok). Such a sweep then crosses the stranded block, which shifts its pattern by one place and passes one letter on to the old zone, just as the growing block does (swr_split). The new zone’s irregular edge eats into the stranded block from the right, a little with every such sweep, so for a long run of these sweeps (a good part of the block’s length, but not all of it: a twin simulation finds the disturbance spreading about two cells per pass) the old zone moves exactly as it would on its own, next to an endless block. Kernel (the lemmas) Computed (the argument that combines them, checked against the real orbit at every such sweep so far).

At zone step 3·107 the parts are: old zone 53 letters, stranded block 8,397, new zone 79. The old zone alone is a tiny system with one tick per sweep that gets through: run alone, the old zone has no reset and no halt in 8,397 ticks, more than the block can shield it for (c/z1.c in the folder of 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1LA1LC_---1LA). In 3·1010 sweeps after zone step 3·107 only 23 sweeps got through the new zone, at the same sweep numbers for 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1LA1LC_---1LA, 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1RA1LC_---1LA and 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD1RB_1LF0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB, whose new zones are the same. Computed

The layers below the zone orbit are all proved. The two-zone picture is not yet a proof, and nothing here decides the machine: a halt needs a sweep through the new zone, the stranded block and the old zone, all the way to the left end. Sweeps that get through the new zone came about 7 times per factor of 10 in the number of sweeps; if that goes on, the next sweep that could reach the left end is something like 101200 sweeps or more away. Heuristic Deciding the machine needs a proof about the zone orbit itself: that the new zone never lets a sweep through often enough, or that the old zone never halts whatever it is fed.

sections.heading: A period at a time
html: <div class="col">

The cells nearest the block are periodic, and a cell is back to its bit after a list of events or after two copies of it. So the events that reach a cell during the first 3·2d sweeps can be built cell by cell, one or two passes per cell, without running the sweeps one by one. The window doubles at about two cells in five while the lists grow by about 7% per cell. Lean proves the method (wfold_run) and runs it by compiled evaluation: nothing leaves the word for 3·263 sweeps, so no halt in the first 1.5·1039 steps. Kernel Native The C engine goes to 3·277 sweeps. Computed

Two things grow with the logarithm of the time, plotted below. Behind a front the stream is disturbed and loses about a fifth of its events per cell; past the front only background is left, and it crosses the stranded block without loss. Every event that has reached the old zone is background, so the old zone has so far moved exactly as alone. The front moves about 3.3 cells per doubling of the window, the background events into the old zone come about 1.35 per doubling. At those speeds the front reaches the old zone at d ≈ 2,600, after about 3,500 background events, fewer than the 9,947 the old zone alone needs to let a sweep through. Heuristic

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1LD_1RC0RC_1LD1RB_1LF0LE_0LA1LE_---1LB: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F; it is this table started in state E

family: Counter zone beside a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a lone 1 at the left end of the tape
summary: A zone of about a hundred cells is rewritten like a counter by passes coming from a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a pass that reaches a lone 1 at the left end of the tape. The last arrival at the left end was at step 143,858,957; no halt in 10^11 steps.
